walkthrough:
Find the median wind speed for Bronlea from its $14$ ordered observations:

$$\text{Median} = \dfrac{22 + 24}{2} = 23\text{ km/h}$$

teacher_walkthrough:
To find the median for Bronlea, note that there are $n = 14$ daily readings. The median position is:
$$\frac{n + 1}{2} = \frac{14 + 1}{2} = 7.5$$
Thus, the median is the arithmetic mean of the 7th and 8th ordered values:
$$\text{7th value} = 22\text{ km/h}, \quad \text{8th value} = 24\text{ km/h}$$
Calculate the average:
$$\text{Median} = \frac{22 + 24}{2} = \frac{46}{2} = 23\text{ km/h}$$

To find the interquartile range for Rogate, split the $14$ ordered values into lower and upper halves of $7$ values each:
$$\text{Lower half: } 4, 5, 7, 7, 10, 11, 13$$
The median of this lower half (the 4th value) is the lower quartile:
$$Q_1 = 7\text{ km/h}$$
$$\text{Upper half: } 15, 16, 18, 23, 23, 26, 34$$
The median of this upper half (the 11th value overall) is the upper quartile:
$$Q_3 = 23\text{ km/h}$$

Start with the definition of the interquartile range:
$$\mathrm{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$$
Substitute the quartile values:
$$\mathrm{IQR} = 23 - 7 = 16\text{ km/h}$$
Therefore, Bronlea median is $23\text{ km/h}$ and Rogate IQR is $16\text{ km/h}$.
